lines.trans: Look at our small wooden sign for the street gate—short, warm, and easy to read.
Read it aloud for me, Nour, so I hear how a neighbour hears it.
"Room Nine Garden Café — Fresh Soup, Warm Bread, Lemon Tart & Tea — Open Daily."
And underneath in smaller letters: "Friday Piano Tea at Six O'Clock."
My aunt's exact Friday hour right on the gate! That makes me proud.
I also wrote the four prices clearly in big numbers so nobody has to squint.
Even without glasses I can read those numbers from two metres away!
Did you leave a small basket by the door for neighbourhood book sharing?
Right beside the piano—all those clean travel books from the hallway bookcase!
A public café, a neighbourhood reading corner, and live music—every word of the city rule!
Let me go practice the waltz once through while Salma bakes the tart shells.
I will carry these menu cards into the kitchen and check on Salma!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Comparative/superlative elative of صغير ('small/young'); invariant in spoken comparative use.

examples.text: تحت الاسم كتبنا السطر التاني بحروف أصغر.
examples.trans: Underneath the name we painted the second line in smaller letters.

examples.text: المرتبان الأصغر مخصص لملح البحر الخشن.
examples.trans: The smaller jar is reserved for coarse sea salt.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

اضطر.gloss: to have to; be forced to

meanings.en: to have to; be forced to
meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb ('have to do something').

examples.text: ما رح يضطر حدا يضيق عيونه عشان يقرأ اللوحة.
examples.trans: Nobody will have to squint to read the sign.

examples.text: اضطرينا ندهن الشيش جوا الممر بسبب المطر.
examples.trans: We had to paint the shutters inside the hallway because of the rain.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian verb taking على ('check on someone/something') or عن ('feel reassured').

examples.text: خليني أطلع عالدرج وأطمن عالشباك العلوي.
examples.trans: Let me step up the ladder and check on the upper transom.

examples.text: اطمنا لما شفنا سلمى بتحرك أصابع رجلها.
examples.trans: We felt relieved when we saw Salma wiggle her toes.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: As a noun after على (على بعد عشر أمتار 'at a distance of ten metres'); distinct from preposition بعد ('after').

examples.trans: The shop is five minutes away.
The stop is a hundred metres away.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Form V verb taking على for practicing music or a craft.

examples.trans: Can I practice the whole song on the piano?

examples.text: مدام سعاد تمرنت ساعة كاملة قبل شاي المساء.
examples.trans: Madam Suad practiced for a full hour before evening tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a garden or yard; a small one is a جنينة, the formal word is حديقة.

examples.trans: We have a small garden behind the house.
The children are playing in the garden.

meanings.note: Used to mean 'even' (e.g., even he went) or 'until' (e.g., until tomorrow).

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حروف.

examples.trans: Two small letters are written on the corner.
The letters of her name are clear on the zip.

meanings.note: Vocalized with fatha-shadda to distinguish adjective حَيّ ('live/living') from noun حي ('neighbourhood').

examples.text: يوم الجمعة رح يكون عنا شاي وموسيقى حية عالبيانو.
examples.trans: On Fridays we'll have tea and live music on the piano.

examples.text: الساحة صارت حية ودافية بوجود الجيران.
examples.trans: The courtyard came alive and warm with the neighbours there.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسعار.

examples.trans: Tonight the room is at half price.
The shop's prices are fair and reasonable.

meanings.note: كتب السفر are travel books; على سفر means 'away travelling'.

examples.trans: I love travelling by bus.
My brother is away travelling this week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سلال.

examples.trans: I put the yellow lemons in the basket.
He tossed the paper into the wastebasket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'easy to do'.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة سهلة وبتجهز بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: This recipe is easy and comes together in half an hour.

examples.text: سهل نرتب الكراسي بعد ما يخلص الدهان.
examples.trans: It will be easy to arrange the chairs once the painting is done.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: With ب- forms بشرط ('on condition that / provided that').

examples.text: بجي معكم بشرط نشرب شاي سوا.
examples.trans: I will come with you provided we drink tea together.
We read all the conditions of the contract clearly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شوربات.

examples.trans: Here is a cup of hot vegetable soup.
Hot soup is wonderful on a rainy day.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Form II verb disambiguated with shadda from adjective ضيق ('narrow').

examples.text: الخط كبير وواضح، ما حدا رح يضيق عيونه.
examples.trans: The lettering is big and clear—nobody will squint their eyes.

examples.text: مازن ضيق عيونه وهو يقرأ الرقم من آخر الساحة.
examples.trans: Mazen squinted as he read the number from across the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used for fresh food, produce, or bread.

examples.text: خبز سلمى طازة وسخن كل صبح.
examples.trans: Salma's bread is fresh and hot every morning.

examples.text: اشترينا ليمون طازة ونعنع أخضر من السوق.
examples.trans: We bought fresh lemons and green mint from the market.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: What is that loud sound upstairs?
The wooden ceiling is high and sunny.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عامة, plural: عامين); الشارع العام means 'main street / public road'.

examples.text: عالشارع العام برا في ضجة سيارات.
examples.trans: Out on the main road there is traffic noise.
A public park near the quarter.

meanings.note: Used for baking dough.

examples.trans: The bread dough is ready in the oven.
She left the dough to rest half an hour.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

علطول.gloss: right away; straight; all the time

meanings.en: right away; straight; all the time
meanings.note: Contracted spoken spelling of على طول ('immediately / straight ahead / always').

examples.text: جيبي كيس تلج علطول وحطيه عالكاحل.
examples.trans: Grab an ice pack right away and put it on the ankle.

examples.text: امشي علطول لآخر الممر بتلاقي غرفة الشمس.
examples.trans: Walk straight down to the end of the hall and you'll find the sunroom.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; also used in the delighted Jordanian exclamation يا عيني! ('oh my! / how lovely!').

examples.trans: Close your eyes and smell the coffee!
Oh my, look at that warm light in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Takes بـ ('proud of someone or something').

examples.text: أنا فخور فيكم واحد واحد عالشغل المتقن.
examples.trans: I'm proud of every single one of you for the careful work.

examples.text: نور كانت فخورة بلوحة البوابة اللي رسمتها.
examples.trans: Nour was proud of the gate sign she lettered.

meanings.note: A written list or a restaurant menu; with -i it is قائمتي, 'my list'.

examples.trans: I wrote the shopping list before the market.
May I have the menu?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قراءات.

examples.trans: We put a brass reading lamp by the desk.
I love reading in the quiet courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Adjective for short in length, height, or time.

examples.text: بعتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
Start with three short, clear sentences.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أمتار.

examples.trans: The table is ten metres away.
The courtyard is eight metres wide.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Form III verbal noun of شارك ('share/take part in').

examples.text: هاد البيانو انصنع لمشاركة الموسيقى مع الناس.
examples.trans: This piano was made for sharing music with people.

examples.text: شكرا إلكم كلكم على مشاركتكم بتجهيز الكافيه.
examples.trans: Thank you all for taking part in getting the café ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفتوحة, plural: مفتوحين).

examples.trans: Is the hardware shop open right now?
Here is to neighbours and our open gates!

meanings.note: Formal/signboard Arabic word for 'café' (alongside conversational كافيه), ideal for painted signs.

examples.text: كتبنا عاللوحة: مقهى جنينة الغرفة تسعة.
examples.trans: We painted on the sign: Room Nine Garden Café.

examples.text: المقهى رح يفتح يوميا من الصبح للمسا.
examples.trans: The café will be open daily from morning till evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مكتبات.

examples.trans: There are old bookshops in downtown Amman.
The public library is a quiet place to read.

meanings.note: An inside hallway or a narrow passage between buildings.

examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
The hallway is dark, turn on the light.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: We found an old music book in the suitcase.
Gentle music is soothing in the evening.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; بوضوح means 'clearly'.

examples.trans: I can hear you clearly on the phone now.
He explained the idea with complete clarity.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
